name: Riding without a helmet
mva_section: Section 194D read with Section 129, Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (inserted by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019, w.e.f. 1-9-2019; the operative word was changed from 'punishable with a fine' to 'liable for a penalty' by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 (Act 8 of 2026), s.2 and Schedule, w.e.f. 15-8-2026 — the rupee amount is unchanged)
description: Section 129 requires every person above four years of age who drives, rides or is carried on a motorcycle in a public place to wear protective headgear conforming to standards prescribed by the Central Government, with an exemption for a Sikh wearing a turban. Section 194D imposes a penalty on riding or allowing a motorcycle to be ridden in contravention of Section 129. Since 15 August 2026 the section is worded as a civil penalty ('liable for a penalty') rather than the earlier criminal-fine wording, following the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026's economy-wide decriminalisation of minor offences — the ₹1,000 amount and the three-month licence disqualification are unchanged. Section 206(4) separately obliges the officer to seize the driving licence and forward it to the licensing authority.
base_fine_text: ₹1,000 fine and disqualification from holding a driving licence for three months
repeat_fine_text: ₹1,000 — Section 194D fixes a single amount and does not prescribe a higher figure for repeat offences; the Delhi Traffic Police schedule likewise shows ₹1,000 for first and subsequent offences
licence_impact: Section 194D expressly disqualifies the rider from holding a licence for three months, and Section 206(4) requires the police officer to seize the driving licence and send it to the licensing authority for disqualification or revocation proceedings under Section 19.

faqs.q: Does the pillion rider also get a challan without helmet?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 129 applies to every person above four years of age driving, riding or being carried on a motorcycle, so a pillion rider without a helmet is covered. A separate provision, Section 194C, punishes violation of the safety measures in Section 128 with ₹1,000 and a three-month licence disqualification — Delhi books triple riding on a two-wheeler under that section.

faqs.q: Is a Sikh wearing a turban exempt from the helmet rule?
faqs.a: Yes. The first proviso to Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 states that the section does not apply to a person who is a Sikh if, while driving or riding a motorcycle in a public place, he is wearing a turban.

faqs.q: Can I be challaned if my helmet is not BIS-certified or the strap is loose?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 129 defines protective headgear as a helmet that both affords a reasonable degree of protection by its shape, material and construction and is securely fastened to the head by straps. Delhi's published schedule lists 'Helmet w/o strap or strap not tied' and 'Defective helmet (not conforming BIS)' as separate ₹1,000 offences under Section 194D.

statute_quote.text: …liable for a penalty of one thousand rupees and he shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months.
statute_quote.attribution: Section 194D, Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as substituted by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2026 (Act 8 of 2026), s.2 and Schedule, w.e.f. 15-8-2026)
